symptom: Three describe outputs check refused (mendixlabs/mxcli#1407): `format (decimalPrecision: -1)` -> "extraneous input '-'"; text box `DecimalPrecision: -1` -> "DecimalPrecision must be a non-negative integer" [MDL-WIDGET18] + [MDL-WIDGET42]; import mapping `root (Wrapper)` -> "extraneous input '('".
cause: propertyValueV3 had no signed number, so `-1` fell to the generic expression alternative (WIDGET42) or was unparseable inside a format block; both validators hard-coded n >= 0 although Studio Pro stores -1 for no fixed precision. schemaRootClause dropped the (Object)/(Array) markers but not a primitive array's (Wrapper) item, so a mapping rooted there printed the marker as a member path.
insight: Decide the wrong side by asking whether the printed value is real: -1 is a stored Studio Pro value (mx check 11.6.6: 0 errors for both widgets), so the grammar and check were wrong, not the describer; the existing 'negative precision' test had asserted -1 is refused without measuring it. For (Wrapper) the opposite holds — a generated marker is never member syntax, and the writer already steps from an array into its (Wrapper) via arrayItemOf, so omitting the clause re-creates the same root. Related, not fixed here: mxcli's own JSON-structure builder writes a ROOT primitive array's item at (Array)|(Object) as a Value, not (Array)|(Wrapper), so a mapping over an mxcli-built root primitive array cannot be authored; unmeasured against Studio Pro.
